items.name: Milestone adherence
items.good: Milestones met or projected to be met on baseline dates; any slip under one week with no downstream impact.
items.medium: One milestone slipped one to three weeks, or a slip is forecast, with a recovery plan agreed.
items.poor: Slip over three weeks, multiple milestones slipped, or a committed client date missed or at risk without a plan.

items.name: Dependency and blocker management
items.good: Blockers identified early, owned, and cleared within the agreed window.
items.medium: Open blockers with named owners and dates, some ageing beyond one sprint.
items.poor: Blockers unowned, recurring across meetings, or dependent on parties not engaged.

items.name: Forecast reliability
items.good: Burn and velocity consistent with plan; estimates have held across recent periods.
items.medium: Forecast revised once with reasons understood.
items.poor: Repeated re-forecasting, unknown effort to complete, or forecast contradicted by later evidence.

items.name: Scope stability and change control
items.good: Scope baselined; changes go through formal change requests and are approved before work starts.
items.medium: Pending change requests or informal requests being absorbed, but tracked.
items.poor: Untracked scope growth, work started on unapproved changes, or disputed scope.

items.name: Deliverable quality and defect trend
items.good: Defects within agreed thresholds and trending down; no critical defects open.
items.medium: Defect count elevated or flat, with a remediation plan; no unresolved critical defects past SLA.
items.poor: Critical defects open past SLA, defect trend rising, or rework impacting schedule.

items.name: Client acceptance and sign-off
items.good: Deliverables accepted on schedule with formal sign-off.
items.medium: Sign-off delayed for administrative reasons or with minor conditions.
items.poor: Deliverables rejected, sign-off withheld for quality or scope reasons.

items.name: Client engagement and sentiment
items.good: Client stakeholders attend, respond, and express confidence.
items.medium: Mixed signals, reduced attendance, or isolated concerns raised.
items.poor: Explicit dissatisfaction, escalation by the client, or disengagement of key sponsors.

items.name: Team capacity and staffing stability
items.good: Team staffed to plan; no unplanned attrition; workload sustainable.
items.medium: Gaps being backfilled, overtime reported, or a single key-person risk.
items.poor: Unplanned exits of critical roles without backfill, or sustained overload affecting delivery.

items.name: Risk and escalation governance
items.good: RAID log maintained and reviewed; escalations raised promptly to the right forum.
items.medium: Risks known but log stale, or escalations raised late.
items.poor: Material risks not logged, escalations missed, or governance forums not held.
